summary: Tested PDF upload for 'Read a document' end to end, backend and frontend. New file tests/test_pdf_upload.py: 17/17 pass. It covers the synthetic sample PDF (200 for the demo, 404 for a registered user), refusals (scanned PDF, non-PDF named .pdf, over 10 MB, corrupt PDF, bad kind, blank label; all 422 with no source stored), and a typed 2-page Redwood PDF read with the real LLM. The read gave page_count=2 and a file_id. Every fact has a page and line (price at page 2, line 1). Values: price 12800, capacity 1/2/4 for weeks 1/2/3, max 10, advance 10. No capacity came from '2-man crew'. Customer = Harborview Credit Union; payer = Brightline. Download: organizer gets 200 application/pdf starting %PDF, partner (redwood) gets 403, organizer from another visitor sandbox gets 404. Applying the PDF readings updated the intake (Redwood capacity [1,2,4], price 1280000 cents). Regression tests test_extract_summary.py and test_assemble_flow.py: 36/36 pass. UI (Playwright, desktop): the sample PDF button shows read-pdf-chosen with the filename and '1 KB', and fills kind=quote, label and date. read-pdf-remove brings the textarea back. Choosing a .docx shows the unsupported-type error in read-errors. Choosing a .pdf through read-file-input works. read-submit-button reads it. The source line shows 'PDF, 2 page(s)'. Readings show 'page N, line M'. source-download opens a new tab and GET /file returns 200 application/pdf (headless Chromium saves the PDF as a download instead of showing it). Select all + Use selected readings sets every fact to applied. No page errors.

minor.issue: An empty label falls back to the filename, so there is no 422 for a missing label. Only a whitespace-only label returns 422. This may be intended, but it differs from the review request.
put_object runs before db.files.insert_one, and there is no cleanup if the insert or a later step fails. This can leave orphan objects in storage. Low risk.

integration_issues.issue: The PDF opens as a blob: URL with a UUID name. If the browser downloads PDFs instead of showing them, the user gets '<uuid>.pdf', not the original filename. The about:blank tab also stays open. Possible fix: build a File with the original name, or use an <a download> fallback.

issues: The sticky readings bar (Select all / Use selected readings) sits at the bottom of the viewport over the form and readings. It covers the Read document button area until you scroll. Minor.

action_items: Optional: decide whether a missing label on PDF upload should return 422 or fall back to the filename (it falls back now)
Optional: keep the original filename when opening or downloading the PDF from a blob
Optional: delete the stored object if the file record insert fails
critical_code_review_comments: locate() line numbers for PDFs are relative to the page and skip the [Page N] marker line correctly (the first content line = line 1). Verified.
The scanned-PDF check (fewer than 20 non-whitespace chars after removing markers) runs before storage, so nothing is stored. Verified.
The download route scopes by project_id; partners are blocked by get_project (403), and other sandboxes get 404. Verified.
seed_data_creation: Per-run demo visitor sandboxes (pdf-<hex>), plus one registered test_<hex>@example.com user for the non-synthetic sample-pdf 404 check.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest /app/backend/tests/ (xdist loadscope; use -n 0 for one file). test_pdf_upload.py makes 1 real LLM read (about 5s). It uses pdf_sample.make_pdf and redwood_quote_pdf from /app/backend. GET /api/project returns sheet.project.rev, not sheet.rev. In headless Playwright, the source-download PDF arrives as a download event on the new tab.
